title: ProofPack egress schema
description: Everything that may ever leave the customer's machine (D1 section 6). At launch the runner makes at most one outbound call: the telemetry POST, a document matching $defs/telemetry. The proofpack-aggregates/1 branch is the shape of the deferred narrative call and of the demo's optional narrative: no code path sends it at launch, but the engine builds and validates it (src/proofpack/egress) so the k-suppression, pseudonymisation and whitelist rules exist and are tested before the feature. No column names, no counts below bucket level, no metric values and no row-level field are in the telemetry document; no row-level field exists anywhere in this schema; no free-text declaration field (justification, description, source) has a place in it. Every string property carries an enum, a const or a pattern with a maximum length, and every object closes with additionalProperties false, so a key or a string the schema does not name cannot pass. Published verbatim on the trust page (build day 8, A-P2).

telemetry.description: The one document the runner sends, at the end of `proofpack run`, after run.json is written; skipped entirely (no socket, no name lookup) with --offline or egress.telemetry: false in criteria.yaml. The ten keys are D1 section 6's literal payload. A HALT writes no document and sends nothing, so halt_code is null on every document the engine sends today; the key and its enum are kept so the shape D1 names is the shape the site stores.

licence_id.description: The id of the licence file the run verified (the site issues lic_ + 32 hex; the pattern admits the prefix plus up to 60 letters or digits so a hand-signed id keeps the shape). Null when no licence file was found or the file was refused, so an unverified id from a tampered file is never reported as if it were a licence.

platform.description: sysconfig.get_platform() plus the CPython tag, as the manifest records it: linux-x86_64-cp312, win-amd64-cp314, macosx-14.0-arm64-cp312.

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON bytes of run.json's manifest block (proofpack.manifest.canonical_json). A pointer to a local record; it reveals nothing about the table.

metric_id.description: Equals criteria_schema.json $defs/metric_id (D1 section 4.3); tests/test_egress.py holds the two enums equal.

method.description: Equals output_schema_v1.json $defs/method plus null (a suppressed cell); the same test holds them equal.

identifier.description: A canonical attribute name or an operating-point id (D1 section 6 header whitelist ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$); an original header never matches because it is never looked at.

level.description: A pseudonym (Site A, Device A, Protocol A, Level A ... Level ZZ), the engine's own Unknown/missing row, or a short token such as F, M or an age band 40-65. Anything else is pseudonymised before it gets here (src/proofpack/egress/pseudonymise.py).

number.description: The egress projection of an engine Number: est, ci_lo, ci_hi, method, n, k, suppressed and nothing else (no flags, no ci_level, no reason text). A suppressed cell carries null in every value field.

two_by_two_cell.description: One 2x2 table (overall per operating point). Suppressed as one cell when n, events (tp + fn) or non-events (fp + tn) fall below the thresholds.

calibration_bin.description: One decile bin of the calibration curve: its size, its events, the mean prediction and the observed proportion. Suppressed as one cell.

x-proofpack.suppression_rule: Any cell with n < min_n, events < min_events or non-events < min_nonevents is serialised with suppressed=true and null values. Customers may only tighten these.
suppression_cells: every Number, on its own n and, where it carries them, k and n - k or n_pos and n_neg; a Number whose n is unknown is suppressed
x-proofpack.pseudonym_order: within each attribute, the original labels sorted by Unicode code point receive Site A, Site B, ... Site Z, Site AA ...; the Unknown/missing row keeps its engine label; a level of any other attribute that is not a short token (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]{0,15}$) is pseudonymised the same way with the Level prefix; the map is written to <out>/pseudonyms.json locally and never serialised into any payload
never_serialised: level labels of site, device, protocol and attr_* columns
